sources.name: TrackNetV3
sources.what: Ball tracker that looks at 3 consecutive frames and outputs a heat map of where the ball is.
sources.use: Our ball tracker. Vendored in third_party/TrackNetV3 with 3 small patches (loading, empty clips, detection threshold).

sources.name: deadfast beach-volley-vision weights
sources.what: TrackNetV3 weights fine-tuned on beach volleyball.
sources.use: Starting point for our ball tracker. Fine-tuned on our own footage with automatic labels (ball v1): recall in an unseen gym went from 0.32 to 0.66.

sources.name: VballNet dataset
sources.what: About 29,000 hand-labelled ball positions from indoor amateur gym footage, the closest public match to our camera.
sources.use: Added to training for ball v2: more recall (0.73 to 0.90 on Kent 2) but a little less precision, so v1 stayed the default.

sources.name: fast-volleyball-tracking-inference: VballNet models
sources.what: Ready-made indoor ball trackers (VballNetV4c, VballNetGridV3).
sources.use: Benchmarked against ours on clicked frames: as good or better overall (GridV3 precision 0.89–0.97), none best everywhere. Candidate ball source for touch detection.

sources.name: fast-volleyball-tracking-inference: RAVEL-VB
sources.what: Player and ball detector with tracking, runs on the CPU (OpenVINO).
sources.use: Compared with YOLO11 on 3 sets: slightly more full-side frames on Kent (19–22% vs 16%) but it collapsed on the 60 fps set (0%, 69 ids per side per rally). Not chosen.

sources.name: Ultralytics YOLO11 + ByteTrack
sources.what: General person detector with a multi-object tracker. Not in the reference list.
sources.use: Our player tracker on all 11 sets. Weak spots: far-side players hidden behind near ones, and many id switches.

sources.name: SportsMOT
sources.what: Player tracks (not just boxes) for basketball, volleyball and football: about 29k volleyball frames, with a sports tracker baseline (MixSort).
sources.use: Planned for better player tracking (fewer id switches). Needs a CodaLab account: sign up yourself, then Participate → Get Data.

sources.name: VolleyVision (Roboflow sets)
sources.licence: AGPL-3.0 (repo LICENSE; README says CC BY-NC-ND)
sources.what: Player, ball, action and court-segmentation image sets, mostly from other camera angles.
sources.use: Its YOLOv8m action detector (models/volleyvision/actions_yv8m.pt) checks whether the receivers played each serve (vball serving). It sees the far team, facing the camera, far better than the near team's backs.

sources.name: ddecks beach-volley-vision
sources.what: Beach volleyball pipeline: ball-visibility rally state machine, serve detection, RF-DETR player detector with ByteTrack.
sources.use: Read 2026-10-06: no per-player stats; its serve side by court depth + trajectory is the idea we tested (serving end right on 94% of clear Kent 3 rallies, see docs/results/phase2e). RF-DETR stays the candidate for low cameras.

sources.name: Ibrahim et al. Volleyball dataset
sources.what: 4,830 broadcast clips with player boxes and 9 individual / 8 group actions.
sources.use: Not used: broadcast side view, far from our camera behind the baseline.

sources.name: Court-Keypoint-Detection
sources.what: YOLO11 court keypoints trained on back-view gym cameras, the right viewpoint for automatic calibration.
sources.use: No published weights, data or licence, so court calibration is clicked by hand (with the magnifier), or drafted from a sister set (vball courtcopy).

sources.name: Roboflow single-image ball sets
sources.what: Ball boxes on single images.
sources.use: Our tracker needs consecutive frames, so single images cannot train it.

sources.name: WASB (Widely Applicable Strong Baseline)
sources.what: Small-ball detection baseline across 5 sports, including volleyball.
sources.use: Not tried; our tracker plus VballNet already cover the ball.

sources.name: VNL-STES
sources.what: 6,137 frame-accurate events (serve, receive, set, spike, block, score) in 1,028 broadcast rallies.
sources.use: Read 2026-10-06: serve 17%, receive 25%, set 23%, spike 22%, block 9%, score 4% of 6,137 events; 74–77% spotting within 1–4 frames; 13 GB, no published weights. Kept for touch spotting (phase 2c).

sources.name: MultiSports (volleyball subset)
sources.what: 12 volleyball action classes with player tubes, broadcast view.
sources.use: Kept for action detection (phase 2c).

sources.name: TU Graz Volleyball Activity 2014
sources.what: 7 action classes with player boxes per frame.
sources.use: Kept for action detection (phase 2c).

sources.name: VREN
sources.what: Rally notation (actions and locations) for pro and NCAA matches.
sources.use: Downloaded (data/external/vren). Reference rates from its 1,498 points: 16% end in a serve error, 5% in an ace, so a 45-point set should have about 7 serve errors and 2 aces. Used to judge vball's serve outcomes and to suggest ace / error for serves still to check.

sources.name: openvolley pydatavolley / ovscout2
sources.what: Read and create DataVolley scouting files from a fixed-camera video.
sources.use: A way to turn scouting into weak labels for actions, if you ever scout a match.

sources.name: T-DEED, E2E-Spot, VideoMAE
sources.what: Precise event-spotting and video-clip models.
sources.use: Candidates for touch / action spotting in phase 2c.

sources.name: passform
sources.what: Ball trajectory turn → contact frame → nearest player = passer, then pose angles.
sources.use: Read 2026-10-06: contact = kink in the ball path, toucher = the person overlapping the ball at that frame. Our flight splits give the kinks; this is the planned touch-attribution rule.
